title: Copyright and Design Registration
subtitle: File a copyright application on Form XIV, clear the discrepancy letter, and register a design that survives a novelty objection.
summary: The two filings everyone assumes are easy, until the discrepancy letter or the novelty objection arrives. Six modules, twelve exercises, both offices covered.
outcomes: Classify a work correctly and identify its owner before you touch the form
Prepare a Form XIV with a Statement of Particulars that does not invite a discrepancy
Obtain and file the Section 45 search certificate for artistic works used as labels
Answer a discrepancy letter inside the thirty-day window
Assess whether a product shape is registrable as a design, and what prior publication kills it
Prepare a design application with correct representations, Locarno class and statement of novelty
Respond to a novelty objection, and know when to switch strategy to a shape mark instead
about: Copyright and design registration are the filings most often handed to the newest person in the room, on the theory that they are simple. They are simple until the Copyright Office sends a discrepancy letter with thirty days to reply, or the Design Wing objects that your representations show two designs, not one.

This course covers both offices end to end, on real applications, discrepancy letters and examination reports. It also covers the question that sits between them and trademark law: for a product shape, which protection do you actually want, and in what order?
It is our shortest course and the one we recommend starting with if you are new to filings.
